spec.description: Where people observe wildlife in Ecuador and the Galápagos, and what they find: research-grade iNaturalist observations read live from the ArcGIS Living Atlas, as H3 cells over the whole record and the most recent observations as dots, with taxonomic, yearly and seasonal breakdowns and the most observed species.

options.content:
## Observed biodiversity in Ecuador

**More than 770,000 research-grade observations** uploaded to
[iNaturalist](https://www.inaturalist.org/) by over 21,000 people, covering
some 24,000 species of mainland Ecuador and the Galápagos. They are read live from the
*Feature Service* [iNaturalist Species Observations](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=996576ae63d4499c924aabea1c3d3768)
in the ArcGIS Living Atlas: **no download and no ETL**, every panel is a query
against the service.

Three things to know so as to read the map properly:

- **The dots are a sample; the hexagons are the total.** The service cuts off at
  10,000 features per request and nothing here pages, so the dot layer is the N
  most recent observations. The H3 cells come already aggregated by the service
  itself and cover them all. The figure to trust is the one in the
  **Observation effort** panel.
- **The hexagons carry no date.** They are historical totals: they follow neither
  the years, the month nor the map's time brush. Everything else does.
- **This measures observation effort, not abundance.** iNaturalist records where
  people go and what they photograph. Quito and the Galápagos stand out for their
  observers as much as for their biodiversity.

To narrow things to a particular area, draw it on the map: the side panels and the
tables obey it. The three charts on the right are filters too: click a group or a
month (click again to clear), or drag across the years.

spec.description: The authoritative numbers for the extent. ArcGIS computes them without paging, so if they ever stop agreeing with the sum of the hexagons, something is truncating. `count_distinct` is refused on this view, so the two counts come from separate requests.
spec.title: Observation effort

params.value: latitude BETWEEN -5.1 AND 1.7 AND longitude BETWEEN -92.0 AND -75.0 AND observed_on_year >= $desdeAnio AND observed_on_year <= $hastaAnio AND observed_on_month IN (${mes:csv})

spec.description: Two datasets with deliberately different reach. The **hexagons** are the H3 cells the service itself publishes pre-aggregated: they cover every observation of the extent, in one request and without paging. The **dots** are the most recent sample.
spec.title: Where things are observed — H3 hexagons and recent observations

spec.rawSql:
-- Observations by group, over the years and month picked (not the group: this chart picks it).
-- Named here so the panel redraws its selection when it changes: $taxon
SELECT grupo, sum(n)::DOUBLE AS n
FROM $cubo
WHERE anio BETWEEN CAST($desdeAnio AS INTEGER) AND CAST($hastaAnio AS INTEGER)
  AND CAST(CAST(mes AS INTEGER) AS VARCHAR) IN ($mes)
GROUP BY grupo ORDER BY n DESC

spec.description: Observations by group over the years and the month picked, in the colours of the map's dots. **Click a bar to filter the dashboard by that group**, click it again to clear (Ctrl- or Shift-click adds a group). It does not filter itself: the other groups stay in grey. Counted in the browser from the cube of group × year × month (Chaski), so it answers at once.
spec.title: Taxonomic composition

spec.rawSql:
-- Context: every observation of the extent or the drawn area, per year.
-- Named here so the panel redraws its brush when they change: $desdeAnio $hastaAnio
SELECT anio::INTEGER AS bin, sum(n)::DOUBLE AS n
FROM $cubo
WHERE anio >= 2016
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

-- What the group and month filters leave, per year (not the years: this chart picks them).
SELECT anio::INTEGER AS bin, sum(n)::DOUBLE AS n
FROM $cubo
WHERE anio >= 2016
  AND grupo IN ($taxon)
  AND CAST(CAST(mes AS INTEGER) AS VARCHAR) IN ($mes)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

spec.description: **Drag across the bars to filter the dashboard by years** ("From year" and "To year"); the bin in the corner goes back to the whole history. Grey is every observation in the extent or drawn area, colour what the group and month leave. It does not filter itself by year. From 2016: before that the service holds few observations.
spec.title: Observations per year

spec.rawSql:
-- Observations by month, for the group and years picked (not the month: this chart picks it).
-- Named here so the panel redraws its selection when it changes: $mes
SELECT CAST(mes AS INTEGER) AS mes, sum(n)::DOUBLE AS n
FROM $cubo
WHERE grupo IN ($taxon)
  AND anio BETWEEN CAST($desdeAnio AS INTEGER) AND CAST($hastaAnio AS INTEGER)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

spec.description: Observations by month of the year, for the group and years picked. It measures **observation effort**, not abundance: it is when people go out to look and to photograph. **Click a month to filter the dashboard by it**, click it again to clear (Ctrl- or Shift-click adds a month).
spec.title: Seasonality

options.content:
**Source** · [iNaturalist Species Observations](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=996576ae63d4499c924aabea1c3d3768),
ArcGIS Living Atlas of the World (Esri), a public service needing no credentials.
Original data from [iNaturalist](https://www.inaturalist.org/), a joint initiative
of the California Academy of Sciences and the National Geographic Society;
each observation keeps the licence whoever uploaded it chose.
The service publishes only *research-grade* observations (`quality_grade =
'research'`: dated, georeferenced, with a photo or sound, and of wild organisms)
and runs roughly **a month behind** the present.
**Extent** · a rectangle (`-92.0 −5.1 → −75.0 1.7`), not the country's border:
it drags in strips of Colombia, Peru and ocean. Real clipping is what the polygon
drawn on the map does.

spec.title: Observed biodiversity — iNaturalist (Ecuador)

spec.description: El id de capa del servicio, interpolado en la **ruta** de la URL. Infinity interpola `url`, así que es la única forma de cambiar de capa: el número de capa es un segmento de la ruta, no un parámetro.

spec.description: Infinity no interpola `columns[].selector`, pero sí `computed_columns[].selector`. El target pide los trece conteos con alias fijos y una columna calculada elige uno bajo el nombre estable `n`, que es por el que colorea el `mapConfig` guardado.

spec.description: El servicio corta en 10 000 rasgos por petición (`maxRecordCountFactor` se satura en 5) y aquí no se pagina, así que esto es el tamaño de la muestra de puntos, no el total. El total lo dice el panel «Esfuerzo».

spec.description: Se aplica sobre `observed_on_year`, un entero indexado, en vez de sobre `observed_on`, que es un `TimestampOffset`. Más barato y sin líos de husos horarios. Los hexágonos no lo siguen: son totales históricos.

spec.name: desdeAnio

spec.description: The last year counted, inclusive; 9999 is no upper bound. The "Observations per year" chart writes it, with "From year", when you drag across its bars. Like "From year", it is compared with `observed_on_year` and the hexagons do not follow it.

Es variable de consulta y no textbox porque al limpiar un filtro de kepler `useVariableSync` escribe el literal `$__all`, y con varios valores escribe un array: un textbox no admite ninguno de los dos.
